role: Sharpen engine juror (senior X ghostwriter and copy chief)
verdict: The app's Claude path trails Typefully slightly. It is safer: 0 facts or meanings changed on 120 new lines, 47/47 sharp lines left alone, and all six broken or meaning-changing engine lines repaired. But it is too timid on lines that need work: 83.3% postable overall and 72.6% on needs-work lines, because stacked hedges, delaying frames and IMHO survive, and the better edit often sits in alt 2. The on-device engine (homepage demo and app fallback) is 66.7% / 49.3% with 15 misses, including 4 broken sentences shown under 'Why it hits', which is an open P0 for the homepage demo; it caps score_ondevice, not the app score, because Claude replaced all four in the app.
to_95: Prompt: replace the absolute 'never drop I think' rule with 'keep one hedge per clause; keep every hedge on a forecast, plan or price call'. Let a frame stand in for 'I think' ('Hot take: I think' -> 'Hot take:'), collapse 'could maybe' to 'could' and 'I think ... probably' to one hedge, and treat 'ngl'/'Not gonna lie' like 'honestly'. Re-run the 120: u-1, 4, 5, 12, 29, 32, 82, 88, 104 and 110 should become h.

Prompt: when a passing alt only drops a delaying frame or preamble, make it version 1 (u-1, 21, 69, 106, 111), and never call a line 'Already sharp' when the why goes on to say what would make it a hook (u-29, 32, 35).

Receipts: derive say/why from the actual diff, not move names. No 'Gave it an end' for an added comma (u-21), no 'Asked, then answered' for 'who knows?' (u-12), no 'run-up is gone' when the line opens on the run-up (u-106), no 'the 4x comes first' or '16:8 and 90 days open the line' when they don't (u-7, u-80).

App: when Claude says 'already sharp' after the engine edited the line, put the writer's line back by default and offer the engine's edit under Another. Today the engine's edit stays and a 6 s toast offers 'Put mine back', so u-18's 'I don't sell' tense change survives by default.

Rules fallback: when every Claude version is rejected, run the engine's line through a stricter guard and ship the draft unchanged ('Couldn't sharpen this safely') instead of an awkward rewrite (u-31 'I'm a founder. Basically always talk…').

On-device engine (homepage demo, instant line, fallback): add guards for a predicate cut off at the end ('and I'm very.'), a clause with no verb ('and a formula that works.'), a dangling start ('Or anything, but'), a pronoun with nothing to refer to after a question frame is cut ('Their motivation … just me.'), a broken idiom ('sleeping on $X') and a tense change ('I'm not selling' -> 'I don't sell'). Drop any version that trips one, and show 'Nothing to cut' rather than a broken line.
Re-run the 120 at production effort (Opus low) to confirm the stand-in's numbers hold.

issues.where: core.js sharpenLine; concepts/r86/home.html Try box and final input
issues.problem: 4/120 realistic lines come back as broken sentences and 2 change meaning. Broken: u-7 'I closed my $PEPE position today for a 4x and I'm very.', u-52 '…lately, and a formula that works.', u-77 'Or anything, but I just hit a 405 lb deadlift…', u-81 'Their motivation to work out completely disappears in the winter, or is it just me. Anyone else?'. Meaning: u-18 'I'm not selling' -> 'I don't sell' on an already-sharp line, with the receipt hiding the verb change; u-25 'sleeping on $TIA' -> '$TIA: most of you are sleeping rn'. The Try box renders them faithfully under 'Why it hits', with receipts such as 'It now opens on what you came to say'. A visitor who hits one stops trusting the product.
issues.fix: Add guards to slBroken/slGuard and use them as hard rejects for every version: a copula plus a degree adverb at the end ('I'm very.'), a ', and' followed by a noun phrase with no finite verb, a sentence that starts with 'Or/And/But anything', a sentence that starts with a possessive pronoun after an 'anyone else feel like' frame was cut, a 'sleeping on|bullish on|long on X' idiom split from its object, and any aspect or tense change in a verb the line keeps. If nothing passes, return state 'clean' with an honest why.

issues.where: core.js SHARPEN_AI '# Never - Drop a hedge' and rule 4
issues.problem: The absolute rule never to drop 'I think', plus keeping every frame, leaves stacked hedges and delaying frames on 19 of 73 needs-work lines (26%). Examples: u-4 'I might be wrong, but I think we could', u-32 'I think … was probably', u-88 'Hot take: I think … kind of', u-104 'I feel like … kind of … probably', u-12 'could maybe', u-5 'In my humble opinion … really matters'. The validator already lets 'I think' go on a non-forecast opinion (V3.opts.thinkAll false), so the prompt is stricter than the safety bar requires. This is the main gap to Typefully.
issues.fix: Change the rule to: 'Keep one hedge per clause. On a forecast, plan or price call keep every hedge. A frame that marks an opinion (Hot take:, Unpopular opinion) replaces I think. Collapse could maybe -> could. ngl/Not gonna lie are padding like honestly.' Add two examples: a stacked hedge collapsed, and a hot take with its I think dropped.

issues.where: prompts.sharpen Return section; SHARPEN.fromClaude pick order
issues.problem: Version 1 is often the timid light edit while a passing alt is the post: u-1 (alt drops 'Not gonna lie'), u-21, u-69 ('Founder who struggles…? You might want to consider…'), u-106 ('I was laid off today after 6 years at the company.'), u-111. App users see alt 2 only if they tap Another.
issues.fix: Prompt: 'If a frame or preamble only delays the point, version 1 drops it; the light edit is version 2.' Or in fromClaude: when v1 still starts with a soft run-up (softMarks of kind announce/throat/open/disclaim) and a passing alt starts after it, promote the alt.

issues.where: slExplain / slAIWhy / HK_SAY labels in core.js
issues.problem: 6/120 receipts are untrue or overstated. u-21 says 'Gave it an end' for a comma; u-12 says 'Asked, then answered' for 'who knows?'; u-106 says 'The run-up is gone, so the line starts on “This is a little bit personal”'; u-7 says 'so the 4x comes first'; u-80 says '16:8 and 90 days open the line'. Three lines are called 'Already sharp' while the why lists what would make them a hook (u-29, 32, 35). The 9.5 bar needs true explanations.
issues.fix: Build say labels from the diff only. 'Gave it an end' only when the end punctuation changed; 'Asked, then answered' only when a question mark is followed by an answer sentence. In slAIWhy, reject a why that quotes the line's opening as 'what it starts on' when that text was marked as a run-up. Reject a why that says X 'comes first' or 'opens the line' unless X is in the line's first 5 tokens. Never pair 'Already sharp' with a 'would make it a hook' tip: say 'Nothing to cut' instead.

issues.problem: When the engine edits a line and Claude then answers 'already sharp', the engine's edit stays in the draft and a 6 s toast offers 'Put mine back'. Five of my already-sharp lines are touched by the engine (u-16, 18, 24, 64, 75), and u-18's tense change ('I don't sell') survives by default. Claude's best verdict loses to the weaker engine's edit.
issues.fix: On a Claude 'clean' verdict, restore the writer's line automatically, keep the engine's version one 'Another' away, and toast 'Claude kept your line: <why>' with Undo.

issues.where: server.mjs /api/v1/sharpen rules(); index.html fallback to the engine's line
issues.problem: When the validator rejects every Claude version, the engine's line ships even when it is awkward: u-31 'I'm a founder. Basically always talk to your customers as much as you possibly can.' Its why, 'The line says the same without it', is false. Timeouts, the cap and a missing key leave the engine's instant edit in the draft the same way, broken lines included.
issues.fix: Apply hook-1's stricter guards to the fallback. If the engine's line fails them, or it restructured (a reshape cut) rather than cut padding, return the draft with state 'clean' and 'Couldn't sharpen this one safely. Try Another or edit it yourself.'

issues.area: Policy split between the two engines
issues.where: core.js sharpenLine SOFT kinds vs SHARPEN_AI rules
issues.problem: The homepage demo (on-device) cuts 'Hot take', 'Honest question', 'lol', 'kind of' and 'I think' on opinions, and moves 'Not financial advice' to the end. The app's Claude prompt keeps the frames, the tone words and the hedges, and forbids ending on a disclaimer. A visitor learns one rule on the homepage and the app does the opposite (u-12, 24, 40, 18).
issues.fix: Bring the engine's cut list into line with the prompt: keep the frames listed in rule 4 and the tone words, and keep NFA where the writer put it (or cut it, never move it to the end). Mirror the hedge rule from hook-2.

issues.problem: 7 of the 73 needs-work lines come back unchanged or nearly so (u-6, 34, 45, 57, 69, 89, 102), and the panel says 'It reads clean as it is' or 'no safe move makes it stronger'. Some fluff labels are false: 'so' in 'so tired' is called 'A warm-up word' (u-23), and 'just' in 'I figured I'd just share' is called 'part of what you mean' (u-6).
issues.fix: Add the missing run-up patterns: 'I've put together a list of (some of)', 'I figured I'd (just) share', 'and I can tell you that', 'In this week's issue …, I wanted to talk (a little bit) about', 'it's really(, really) important to', 'you might want to consider'. Classify 'so' before an adjective as an intensifier. When nothing is cut, say 'Nothing safe to cut on-device' rather than 'reads clean'.

issues.problem: The engine's line is written into the draft at once and Claude's replaces it a few seconds later, so broken engine lines (u-7, 52, 77, 81) are visible in the composer before Claude repairs them.
issues.fix: When the engine's line trips a guard (hook-1), don't write it. Show 'Asking Claude…' on the line and wait for Claude, falling back to the draft as written.

issues.problem: The breakage checks miss a predicate cut off at the end ('… and I'm very.') and a ', and' clause with no verb ('…, and a formula that works.'). Claude didn't produce these here, but the validator is the only check between a model slip and the writer's draft.
issues.fix: Add [/\b(?:am|is|are|was|were|i['’]m|it['’]s|we['’]re|they['’]re)\s+(?:very|so|really|too|pretty|quite)\s*[.!?]?\s*$/i, 'cut-off predicate'] and a check that each ', and'/'. And' clause has a finite verb (slFinite).

issues.problem: If data.unchanged is true and a later version equals the draft, the function returns 'clean' even when version 1 was a passing edit.
issues.fix: Return 'clean' for a later identical version only when no earlier version passed (ok.length === 0).

issues.problem: Small changes the writer didn't ask for: 'BREAKING: The' becomes 'BREAKING: the' (u-15), '!!' and '!' become '.' (u-77, u-99, u-30), and a sarcastic 'Really love that for me' loses 'Really' (u-16). For 'asdf test test' the reason given, 'Sharpen needs a few more words', is wrong. Claude's 'This reads as a test, not a hook' is right.
issues.fix: Keep the case after a colon, keep the writer's ! and !!, don't cut an intensifier in the second sentence of a sarcastic echo, and give gibberish its own message.

issues.problem: These Claude lines came from a stand-in at default effort. Production runs Opus 5.5 at low effort with a 12 s timeout, so the shipped rate and the rules-fallback rate may differ.
issues.fix: Re-run the same 120 lines through sharpenClaude with the production tier settings, measuring the timeout rate and the rules fallbacks, before quoting these numbers.
